title: Dynamic NUMA-aware threadpool and bulk request serializer to reduce CPU-side latency
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: production traces and microbenchmarks showed significant CPU-side tail latency attributed to expensive thread pin/unpin sequences and repeated small serializations of request headers when forming continuous batches. This PR introduces two complementary optimizations: 1) a dynamic NUMA-aware threadpool that probes topology at startup and maintains pliable worker groups to avoid frequent expensive task pinning/unpin operations and to reduce cross-node memory traffic; 2) a bulk request serializer that coalesces header/metadata encoding for small contiguous requests into a zero-copy-friendly header slab when safe, falling back to the original path for incompatible payloads. Changes are targeted at the runtime hotpath and designed to be opt-in via runtime flags to simplify rollout. Checklist: - [x] add NUMA probe and topology-aware worker groups - [x] implement dynamic worker affinity policy with low-overhead heuristics - [x] implement bulk-serializer with zero-copy slab and safe fallback - [x] add kvcache hinting to avoid serialized work for cached prefixes - [x] microbench harness + performance tests - [x] e2e smoke tests on dedicated hardware Motivation, design and tradeoffs are inlined in docs/runtime/numa-bulk-serializer.md. Rollout plan: behind feature flag 'runtime.dynamic_numa_bulk_serializer'; staged A/B on canary fleet; fall back to previous threadpool on degraded metrics. Impact summary: p50 generation latency decreased 6-12% across mid-to-long sequences in our internal bench, CPU syscalls related to sched_setaffinity reduced by ~82% on noisy NUMA nodes under bursty load, and end-to-end tail latency (p99) improved by up to 18ms in heavy continuous-batching scenarios. Compatibility: no changes to API surface. The feature is disabled by default. Related work: follows observations from ENG-14522 and complements existing batching work in ENG-14971.

feat(runtime): implement dynamic NUMA-aware worker group and affinity policy
perf(serializer): introduce bulk request serializer and slab allocator
perf(kvcache): add prefix-qualification hints to skip serialization for cache hits
test(perf): add threadpool and serializer microbench harnesses
docs: add runtime design note and rollout instructions
review_comments: Diego Ramirez (reviewer): Nice direction. Please justify why dynamic affinity is preferred over static pin maps in the design doc. Consider fallback when numa info is inconsistent across kernels.
Priya Nair (author): Added section in docs/runtime/numa-bulk-serializer.md explaining decision; dynamic affinity avoids expensive remap operations at runtime and can react to hot-node pressure.
Marta Kline (reviewer): Bulk serializer looks good but edgecases around encrypted payloads need explicit checks. Also, can you avoid allocations in the hotpath?
Priya Nair (author): Bulk-serializer uses a preallocated slab per-worker and validates 'is_contiguous' and 'not_encrypted' flags before coalescing; added unit tests and comments.
Liam O'Connor (reviewer): CI failure on macOS build (clang) — thread APIs used are Linux-specific. Can we gate the probe to only POSIX platforms with sched support?
Priya Nair (author): Gated probe behind #ifdef and added a noop fallback path for macOS and musl; test matrix updated.
Marta Kline (reviewer): Left a few small nits around comments and naming; approve after those are fixed.
Diego Ramirez (reviewer): Verified perf numbers on canary cluster and approve.
Repo Maintainer (merge): squashed and merged after approvals.
ci_checks: perf-regression: bench-sanity — fail (initial run, serializer slab edgecase)
performance_summary: Internal microbench: threadpool_bench shows 30-45% reduction in affinity syscall walltime under bursty load; p50 generation latency decreased 6-12% for sequences 256-1024 tokens; p99 improved by up to 18ms on heavy continuous-batching traffic; kvcache-prefetch hints reduced redundant serialization work by ~28% in mixed workloads.
release_notes: Add dynamic NUMA-aware threadpool and opt-in bulk request serializer. Improvements: lower CPU syscalls, reduced tail latency, and fewer redundant serializations. Disabled by default; enable via runtime.dynamic_numa_bulk_serializer. Rollout: canary -> gradual.
